About

Ningbo, China

I am a songwriter, producer and frontman turned academic, and I study the industry I spent more than a decade working in.

I was principal songwriter, singer and producer of the Sony-signed band Red Light Company, whose album Fine Fascination reached number 13 in the UK and number 24 in Japan. We headlined our own tours and supported The Killers, U2, Coldplay, Kasabian, Kaiser Chiefs, Snow Patrol and Editors. After the band I wrote and produced for other artists, working with Lana Del Rey, Natasha Bedingfield and the producer Flood, and wrote and produced Noemi’s double-gold “Bagnati dal sole”. My music has been placed in film and television including Tin Star, The Royals and Farming.

I left the industry for a PhD at Griffith University, and since 2023 I have taught and researched at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China. UNNC told the story in From singer to assistant professor in Ningbo. I share songwriting and production know-how with more than 45,000 followers on RedNote and BiliBili, still release my own music, and am serialising my first novel, Proofs.

Music

Records, production, film & TV

With Red Light Company I was principal songwriter, frontman and producer. Zane Lowe named “Arts & Crafts” the Hottest Record in the World, several singles were B-listed on BBC Radio 1, and The Sun made “Scheme Eugene” its Single of the Week. NME, HMV and Radio 1’s Edith Bowman all tipped the band for 2009.

After the band I worked as a writer and producer under deals with Notting Hill Publishing and Universal Music Group. That work took in Lana Del Rey, Natasha Bedingfield and Flood, a double-gold single with Noemi, a fifth place at the Sanremo Music Festival, a US iTunes top 10 EP with Laura Welsh, and Joseph J. Jones’s “Gospel Truth” and “Crawl”, which charted on German airplay, made Spotify’s New Music Friday in ten markets and hit viral charts across Europe.

  • #13UK Albums Chart, Fine Fascination, plus #7 on the UK Album Downloads Chart for five weeks
  • #24Japan Albums Chart, Fine Fascination
  • #12UK Physical Singles Chart, “Scheme Eugene”, four weeks
  • 2×Gold for “Bagnati dal sole”: 15,000 physical copies in 2014, reconfirmed with 25,000 downloads in 2016

Academic

Assistant Professor in International Communications, University of Nottingham Ningbo China

Research

Platforms, culture, memory

My research looks at platform capitalism and the cultures that grow inside it: how streaming metrics shape what gets funded, how algorithms rearrange genre, and why people turn back to dead formats.

I work in the School of International Communications at UNNC, where I serve as FHSS Director of Social Media and Communication, and supervise PhD and MA researchers. I am a member of the Digital Heritage Centre, hold a PhD from Griffith University and a BA in Creative Music Technology from the University of Hull, and am a Fellow of the Higher Education Academy.

Platform disruption

Streaming economics, metrics and the timing of cultural investment.

Algorithmic culture

How recommendation algorithms reshape genre and break the lines of influence between musical generations.

Cultural memory

Speculative nostalgia, obsolete media and format revivals.

Participatory culture

DIY production, artist and fan relationships, and work in the attention economy.

Publications

Books, articles, chapters
Monograph

The Music Industry in the Digital Age

How Platforms are Redefining Pop, DIY and Participatory Culture

An account of how digital production tools, social media and streaming have changed the way music is made, distributed and heard. Drawing on interviews with artists, producers and industry professionals, the book follows the rise of the independent artist, the changing jobs of labels and A&R in a data-driven market, algorithmic curation and genre, TikTok virality, and what constant engagement demands of artists, including its toll on mental health.
